_description: Every TRACKED scripts/**/*.mjs that constructs an Anthropic client WITHOUT a literal backend pin. Gate: node scripts/check-anthropic-pins.mjs. Rule A (an unpinned construction in a file whose request carries a param the cli backend cannot serve) is a hard failure no entry excuses. The param question is an ALLOWLIST since 2026-11-15: inside a literal messages.create({...}) argument every key outside model/max_tokens/messages counts, named or not, and elsewhere in the file only a NAMED unserviceable param (system, tools, tool_choice, stream) counts, because outside that argument the scan cannot tell which object is a request. unpinnedConstructions is Rule B, the drift-only record that a human decided each remaining unpinned construction serves only cli-serviceable calls; each entry carries the COUNT of unpinned constructions in that file (a count, not mere presence, so a construction added later cannot ride on an old declaration) and a reason saying what was checked, INCLUDING any client handed to another module, since that handoff is what a file-local scan cannot see. indirectPins is the one escape from Rule A, and it is verified not trusted: the named via function must exist in that file and contain the literal pin. Each entry also carries argsDigest, a digest of that file's unpinned construction ARGUMENTS: the count alone cannot see a REPLACEMENT (swapping one unpinned construction for another preserves the total while the reason goes stale). Two structurally identical constructions produce the same digest by design — e.g. several bare createAnthropicClient() calls — because for this gate they ARE the same shape. The gate PARSES (since 2026-11-15 it uses the shared scripts/lib/ast.mjs, not regexes); its remaining stated limits are a request staged before the call and a dynamic computed member, both of which need dataflow and are documented in the module.

scripts/anthropic-ping.mjs.reason: The reachability ping sends {model, max_tokens, messages} only — no system, tools or tool_choice — and is the one command whose job is to prove the AMBIENT backend works, so pinning it would make it test something other than what the operator configured. Client is not handed anywhere. Audited 2026-11-15 for reliance on `max_tokens` as a HARD bound (the one allowlist entry cli accepts and ignores): it does not rely on one — a reachability probe has no output contract to exceed.

scripts/lib/neighbourhood-query.mjs.reason: The security-failure-mode Haiku call sends {model, max_tokens, messages} only; the JSON contract is in the USER turn, not system. Client is local to the branch and not handed to another module. Audited 2026-11-15 for reliance on `max_tokens` as a HARD bound (the one allowlist entry cli accepts and ignores): it does not rely on one — the ceiling is a cost budget, not a correctness constraint; a longer answer is still parsed.

scripts/lib/visual/explain.mjs.reason: Advisory VLM prose: {model, max_tokens, messages} only, with the instruction in the user content. Client is local; failures already degrade to '' and never block the deterministic report. Audited 2026-11-15 for reliance on `max_tokens` as a HARD bound (the one allowlist entry cli accepts and ignores): it does not rely on one — advisory prose that already degrades to an empty string and never gates.

scripts/symbol-index/summarise.mjs.reason: The highest-volume Claude call site here, and deliberately cli-serviceable: the one-line-per-symbol instruction is in the USER turn, so no system/tools/tool_choice is sent and the Max 20x credit is kept. Truncation is caught by assessBatchCompleteness reading stop_reason, not by max_tokens. Both branches (public and the azureRoute one, which reconcileBackendWithBaseUrl already coerces to sdk) are local; the client is not handed anywhere. Audited 2026-11-15 for reliance on `max_tokens` as a HARD bound (the one allowlist entry cli accepts and ignores): it does not rely on one — truncation is detected by assessBatchCompleteness reading stop_reason, which is the enforcement that matters.

scripts/symbol-index/summarise-domains.m.reason: Same shape as summarise.mjs: {model, max_tokens, messages} only, instruction in the user turn. Client is local to the call. Audited 2026-11-15 for reliance on `max_tokens` as a HARD bound (the one allowlist entry cli accepts and ignores): it does not rely on one — same shape as summarise.mjs; a longer per-symbol line is still a usable summary.

scripts/lib/brainstorm/azure-claude-adap.reason: Pinned backend:'sdk' once in clientOptions(), which both constructions spread, rather than duplicating the literal. This call passes system, so the pin is load-bearing — and the gate re-reads clientOptions() to confirm the literal is still there.
